# site-spec-mcp

> An MCP server that audits a website's machine-readable layer (robots.txt, llms.txt, canonical
> and noindex signals, JSON-LD, Open Graph, response headers, accessibility semantics, trackers
> and cookies) and applies deterministic repairs. Runs the site-spec engine in-process over
> stdio. Node 20+, zero runtime dependencies, no account and no API key.

## What it is

site-spec-mcp gives an agent four tools over a live URL or a local directory of built HTML.
The audit engine is deterministic: no model decides what counts as broken, so two runs on the
same input give the same findings. 40 checks, 17 of which carry an automatic repair.

Use it when you have generated, edited, or been handed a website and need to know whether the
part a browser does not render is correct.

## Install and register

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add site-spec -- npx -y site-spec-mcp
```

Codex, in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.site-spec]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "site-spec-mcp"]
```

Any other MCP client, in `mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "site-spec": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "site-spec-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Tools

- `list_checks` — no arguments. Returns `{ count, fixable, checks[] }`, each check with `id`,
  `description`, `category`, `fixable`. Call this first to learn valid check ids.
- `audit_site` — arguments `url` (required; a URL, a bare hostname, or a local directory path),
  `checks` (optional array of check ids to filter to), `maxPages` (optional, 1-200, default 25,
  live crawls only). Returns `{ ok, target, mode, live, errors, warnings, pages, findings[] }`.
- `fix_issue` — arguments `url_or_path` (required), `check_id` (required, exactly one id),
  `write` (optional boolean, default false), `out_dir` (optional), `maxPages` (optional).
  Returns `{ checkId, fixAvailable, matchedFindings[], actions[], diffs[], written[] }`.
  Default is a dry run: it returns diffs and writes nothing. `write: true` requires a local
  directory target and is refused for a URL, because a remote server is not writable.
- `compile_spec` — arguments `business` (required object: `{ pack, brief, site, spec }`, with
  optional `foundation` and `target`), `out_dir` (optional). Returns `{ ok, pack, spec, files,
  findings }`, and `written[]` when `out_dir` is given.

## Minimal example

```jsonc
// 1. learn the check ids
{ "tool": "list_checks", "arguments": {} }

// 2. audit a live site
{ "tool": "audit_site", "arguments": { "url": "https://example.com", "maxPages": 10 } }

// 3. see the repair for one finding, without writing anything
{ "tool": "fix_issue", "arguments": {
    "url_or_path": "https://example.com",
    "check_id": "audit/robots-blocks-ai-search"
  } }

// 4. apply it to the local build directory that produces that site
{ "tool": "fix_issue", "arguments": {
    "url_or_path": "./dist",
    "check_id": "audit/robots-blocks-ai-search",
    "write": true
  } }
```

## When not to use it

- Rendering, layout, visual design, or CSS. site-spec reads served HTML and headers; it does
  not open a browser and has no opinion about how a page looks.
- Client-rendered content. A live crawl audits the HTML the server returns, so a page whose
  content only exists after JavaScript runs will look empty to it. Audit the built output
  directory instead.
- Performance measurement. There is no Lighthouse run, no Core Web Vitals, no timing.
- Writing to a remote site. Every fix is either a diff or a write to a local directory.
- Authenticated or private hosts. The crawler fetches public HTTP(S) only.
- Content quality, copywriting, or SEO strategy. The checks are mechanical and policy-based.
